q: These shall be provided in smoke barriers at points where the barrier crosses an exit access corridor. It is required for horizontal exit doors.
n: Doors in smoke barriers and horizontal exits must be self-closing or automatic-closing. Source: RIRR of RA 9514 (Fire Code 2019), smoke barrier doors; NFPA 101, Sec. 8.5.4.

q: These doors are typically larger than traditional swinging doors as the weight of these doors are distributed to a central point located at the bottom and top of the door, making a larger door entrance possible
n: Pivot doors turn on top and bottom pivots instead of side hinges, so they can be larger than ordinary swing doors. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (pivot doors).

q: Which door system allows multiple panels to slide along parallel tracks and stack neatly behind one another to create a wide, unobstructed opening?
n: Stacking sliding doors have several panels on parallel tracks that stack behind one another for a wide opening. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (sliding doors).

q: This door with multiple folds is used for wardrobe cabinets
n: Bifold doors, with folding panel pairs, are common on wardrobes. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Which type of door rotates on a vertical axis offset from the frame. allowing for oversized panels and a seamless swing motion often used in high-end architectural entrances?
n: A pivot door rotates on a vertical axis set in from the frame, allowing oversized panels and a smooth swing. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: Emergency exit doors must always swing outward rather than inward. What is the primary reason for this design choice?
o: To improve airflow during evacuation, thus clearing smoke and heat
To minimize building cost as it reduces additional reinforcements
n: Outward-swinging exit doors open with the flow of escaping occupants, so crowd pressure cannot block them. Source: NBC IRR Rule XII, Sec. 1207.3.a; RIRR of RA 9514.

q: What do you call the horizontal element or panel located directly above a door opening and below the lintel, often used for ventilation, light, or decorative detailing?
n: A transom is the panel or window directly above a door, below the lintel, used for ventilation, light or decoration. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: A type of door that has multiple sections which fold into one side of the frame and do not swing in or out to open and close. It is appealing for room configurations where there is less room for a door to open, such as on a balcony or a patio door. It adds value to the property as it can create extra space and have desirable designs.
o: Pivot Door "4D A op M4 E j i
n: Bifold doors fold their panels to one side instead of swinging, which saves space on balconies and patios. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated.

q: A restroom door requires a locking device that provides occupant privacy while still allowing emergency access from the outside when necessary. Which lockset is most appropriate for this application?
n: A privacy lock locks from inside for occupant privacy but has an emergency release from outside. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.2 (privacy function).

q: A frameless tempered glass entrance door in a commercial building requires a concealed door-control mechanism installed within the floor slab. The device must support the door, control its swing, and automatically return it to the closed. position after use. Which hardware performs this function?
n: A floor spring set in the slab supports a frameless glass door, controls its swing and returns it to closed. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.4 (door controls); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door hardware); BHMA/ANSI A156 series.

q: A cabinet door requires a temporary holding device rather than a true mechanical latching system. Which hardware is most appropriate for this application?
n: A magnetic catch holds a cabinet door shut without a mechanical latch. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door hardware); BHMA/ANSI A156 series (cabinet hardware).

q: A cabinet requires a compact locking device commonly used in office furniture, lockers, display cases, and storage cabinets. The mechanism is operated by a key and secures the door by rotating a metal arm behind the frame when turned. Which hardware is being described?
n: A cam lock is a key-operated cabinet lock. Turning the key rotates a metal arm (cam) behind the frame. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.11 (cabinet locks).

q: Which door hardware is specifically engineered to actively regulate closing speed, preventing abrupt impact and eliminating the risk of forceful slamming.
n: A door closer is a hydraulic device that controls the closing speed (and latching) of a door, so the door shuts by itself without slamming. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.4 (Door Controls – Closers).

q: Which type of hinge is commonly used for both vertical and horizontal applications because it runs continuously along the fill length of the member, providing uniform support and load distribution?
n: A piano (continuous) hinge runs the full length of the member, giving uniform support. It is used both vertically and horizontally. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.26 (continuous hinges).

q: Double security for main door
n: A deadbolt adds a second, solid lock on main doors. It cannot be pushed back without the key. Source: ANSI/BHMA A156.36 (auxiliary locks).

q: A coastal residential project requires interior door knobs that must resist corrosion, provide a naturally antimicrobial surface for high-touch areas, and offer a premium tactile feel without the rapid patina formation seen in pure copper. The architect also wants a material that is strong enough to withstand repeated use without deforming. Which material best satisfies these performance requirements for the door knobs?
n: Solid brass resists corrosion, is naturally antimicrobial, feels premium, tarnishes more slowly than pure copper, and is strong enough for heavy use. Source: Copper Development Association (antimicrobial copper alloys); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (door hardware); BHMA/ANSI A156 series.

q: What is the most hygienic material for handrails?
n: Stainless steel is the most hygienic handrail material: non-porous, easy to clean and corrosion-resistant. Source: ASTM A240 (stainless steel); Nickel Institute hygiene data.

q: Also known as Particle Board, it is often confused with Oriented Strand Board, OSB. It is a light and weak fiberboard made appealing by painting or by using wood veneers on visible surfaces.
n: Chipboard (particle board) is often confused with OSB. It is light and weak and usually covered with paint or veneer. Source: ANSI A208.1 (particleboard).

q: Due to its versatility, corrosion resistance, availability and cost-effectiveness, it is used across a wide range of industries and is thus considered the most common type of stainless steel.
n: Type 304 is the most common stainless steel: versatile, corrosion-resistant, available and economical. Source: ASTM A240; Nickel Institute.

q: Which is not a finish for stainless steel
n: Stainless steel finishes include hairline, satin (brushed) and mirror. "Glossy" is a paint sheen, not a stainless finish. Source: ASTM A480 (stainless steel finish designations).

q: You are asked to design a passive-cooling strategy for a remote research out post in Hocos Norte, where daytime temperatures rise sharply but drop significantly after sunset. The client wants the interior spaces to remain thermally stable without relying on mechanical cooling. The design team is evaluating material properties that can absorb excess heat during the day, delay heat transfer, and release stored heat slowly at night to moderate indoor temperature swings. Which material property best supports this passive thermal-stabilization requirement?
n: High thermal mass soaks up daytime heat, delays its transfer and releases it slowly at night. That evens out indoor temperatures where nights are cool. Source: ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 26; Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: An architect is designing a lightweight modular training facility in humid, low-wind conditions in Laguna. The building will be occupied only during daytime and must cool down rapidly after sunset to avoid heat retention that would make evening classes uncomfortable. The client specifically wants a wall system that does not store daytime heat, responds quickly to temperature changes, and avoids the "heat-soak" effect common in concrete structures. Which material property best supports this requirement?
n: Low thermal mass stores little heat and responds quickly, so a daytime-only building cools fast after sunset. Source: Lechner, Heating, Cooling, Lighting.

q: A project team is developing a west-facing training facility in Cavite that experiences intense afternoon solar exposure. The building will be occupied for long stretches during peak heat hours, and the client wants to reduce cooling demand by blocking as much heat as possible from entering the interior. The team is evaluating material properties that slow heat transfer through the wall assembly, regardless of whether the wall stores heat or not. Which material property best meets this requirement?
n: A high R-value (thermal resistance) slows heat flow through the wall, whether or not it stores heat. Source: ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 26.

q: In tropical climates. where cooling efficiency is essential, which insulation material despite having a low initial R-value, becomes highly effective when paired with air cavities to block radiant heat transfer, reducing indoor air temperatures significantly?
n: Reflective foil has little R-value of its own. Facing an air cavity, its low emissivity blocks radiant heat, which dominates roof heat gain in the tropics. Source: ASTM C1313 (radiant barriers); ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 26.

q: Which characteristic of VOCs in insulation is the most harmful in indoor environments?
n: VOCs from insulation are harmful mainly because they degrade indoor air quality. Source: US EPA, Indoor Air Quality—VOCs; ASHRAE Standard 62.1.

q: From among the choices, which insulation is recommended to avoid or minimize asthma episodes?
n: Polyester (PET) insulation has no binders or irritating fibers and emits negligible VOCs, so it suits occupants with asthma. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals, Ch. 26 (insulation materials); manufacturer data; GREENGUARD certification data.

q: Which insulation material prioritizes sustainability by incorporating at least 50% recycled Polyethylene Terephthalate (PET) fibers, while remaining non-irritants, safe to handle, and free of harmful binder chemicals?
n: Polyester insulation contains a high share (often ≥50%) of recycled PET. It is non-irritant, safe to handle and free of chemical binders. Source: ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals, Ch. 26 (insulation materials); manufacturer data.

q: From among the choices, which is NOT suitable for building users with newspaper dust allergies, as it is made from recycled cardboard?
n: Cellulose insulation is made from recycled paper and cardboard. Its dust can trigger reactions in people allergic to newspaper dust. Source: ASTM C739 (cellulosic fiber insulation).

q: The following insulations are made from recycled plastics except?
n: Cellulose insulation is loose-fill or sprayed fiber made mostly from recycled paper (newsprint and cardboard) and treated with fire retardant. It is not made from recycled plastics. Source: ASTM C739 (Cellulosic Fiber Loose-Fill Insulation).

q: Which insulation material offers high thermal efficiency, is lightweight and is commonly used in cost-effective residential and commercial applications, but has limited fire resistance?
n: EPS is light, efficient and cheap, but its fire resistance is limited. Source: ASTM C578 (polystyrene insulation); ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals, Ch. 26 (insulation materials); manufacturer data.

q: Which insulation material provides exceptional moisture resistance, high compressive strength, and is widely used in underground and below-grade applications?
n: XPS has excellent moisture resistance and high compressive strength, so it is used below grade and underground. Source: ASTM C578.

q: In modern insulation applications, concerns about indoor air quality, environmental impact, and sustainable material sourcing have become increasingly important. While various insulation materials offer thermal efficiency, moisture resistance, and fire safety, which option is specifically engineered to reduce VOC emissions, improve indoor air quality, and enhance sustainability, all without compromising performance?
n: Earthwool (Knauf glass wool with ECOSE bio-based binder) is made to cut VOC emissions and improve indoor air quality without losing performance. Source: Knauf Insulation product data; GREENGUARD Gold.

q: Which insulation is best if you want both moisture resistance and fire resistance'?
n: Rock wool is non-combustible (melts above 1,000 °C) and water-repellent. Source: ASTM C612 (mineral fiber insulation).

q: .Which insulation is best if you want soundproofing. thermal regulation and fire safety without using additional treatment?
n: Rock wool insulates heat and sound and is inherently fire-resistant, with no added treatment. Source: ASTM C612; ASHRAE Handbook—Fundamentals, Ch. 26 (insulation materials); manufacturer data.

q: Which wall construction is specifically designed to provide high airborne sound insulation while minimizing wall thickness in modern buildings?
n: Gypsum drywall on studs with rockwool in the cavity gives high airborne sound insulation (STC) with a thin wall. Source: ASTM E90/E413; Egan, Architectural Acoustics.

q: Which wall assembly is most appropriate for soundproofing between adjacent apartment units while maintaining a relatively thin wall profile?
o: Single-layer Gypsum Board on Metal Studs
n: Drywall with rockwool in the cavity gives good STC between units while keeping the wall thin. Source: ASTM E413; Egan, Architectural Acoustics.

q: A recording studio requires maximum airborne sound isolation to minimize sound transmission to adjacent spaces. Which wall assembly is most appropriate?
n: Decoupled double-stud drywall with rockwool gives the most airborne isolation for a recording studio. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (double-stud STC).

q: Which material is primarily used to reduce echoes and reverberation within a music studio?
n: Acoustic foam panels absorb reflections, cutting echo and reverberation inside a studio. Isolation is a separate matter. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics.

q: While sealing a PVC drain pipe penetration in a fire-rated wall, the installer checks the specification and notes that the material must expand when exposed to high heat to close the gap left when the plastic pipe softens. A product such as 3M Fire Barrier Sealant CP 25WB+ is recommended for this condition. What type of material provides this heat-activated expansion?
n: Intumescent sealants expand in fire and close the gap left when plastic pipes soften. Source: ASTM E814 / UL 1479 (firestop systems).

q: During inspection of spray-applied fire-resistive material (SFRM) bags delivered to the site, the inspector notices that one of the lightweight aggregates consists of bright white, popcorn-like granules commonly used to reduce density in fireproofing mixes. Which material matches this description?
n: Perlite is the bright white, popcorn-like expanded volcanic glass used as a lightweight aggregate in fireproofing. Source: ASTM C332 (lightweight aggregates for insulating concrete).

q: Which of the following acoustic materials is generally the Hghtest in weight while oc = Y 5 = providing effective sound absorption?
n: Acoustic foam is the lightest of these absorbers. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics (absorber densities).

q: A building in the Philippines requires insulation primarily to reduce heat gain through the roof while maximizing thermal performance per unit thickness. Which material is most appropriate?
n: Polyurethane foam has the highest R-value per unit thickness of these (about R-6 to R-7 per inch closed-cell). Source: ASHRAE Fundamentals, Ch. 26.

q: Which has the best fire resistance?
n: Rock wool has the best fire resistance: non-combustible and melting above 1,000 °C. Source: ASTM C612; EN 13501-1 (Euroclass A1).

q: Where is the most effective location to install insulation on a concrete roof to reduce thermal bridging, protect the waterproofing layer, and maintain structural temperature stability?
n: Insulation on top of the slab (protected roof) avoids thermal bridging, shields the waterproofing and keeps the structure at a stable temperature. Source: NRCA Roofing Manual (protected membrane roofs); ASHRAE 90.1.

q: In a vaulted ceiling design where the architectural beauty and openness must be preserved, where should insulation be placed to maintain thermal efficiency while allowing the ceiling's structure to remain visible?
n: To keep a vaulted structure exposed, the insulation goes above the roof deck. Source: Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (insulated roof decks).

q: Thin and flexible strips of metal used to separate sheets of drywall from the structure of the building primarily for soundproofing.
n: Resilient channels are thin, flexible metal strips that decouple drywall from the framing for soundproofing. Source: Egan, Architectural Acoustics; ASTM C645.

q: A high-rise condominium in Ortigas is experiencing wide day-to-night humidity swings due to its mixed-mode ventilation system. The developer wants a wood-finish flooring material that will maintain flatness over time, even when units are left unoccupied for weeks with no air-conditioning. The material must minimize surface distortion and movement. Which flooring option is the most appropriate for this condition?
n: Engineered wood (a cross-ply core under a veneer) stays far more dimensionally stable than solid boards through humidity swings. Source: ANSI/HPVA EF (engineered wood flooring); Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: The Philippine Ebony is also known. as?
n: Kamagong (Diospyros blancoi) is known as Philippine ebony. Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: Which of the following is a type of Philippine Mahogany. widely recognized for its durability and strength. making ita preferred choice for construction and furniture- making?
n: Tanguile is one of the woods sold as Philippine mahogany (red lauan group), valued for durability and workability. Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood).

q: Lumber is sold units of?
n: Lumber is sold in even-numbered lengths in feet (8, 10, 12 ft...). Source: Philippine Wood Handbook (FPRDI-DOST); Ching, Building Construction Illustrated (wood); PNS lumber standards.
